message.title: Dash for small gas turbines set to impact data center costs
message.body:
September 28 - Demand for small open cycle and aeroderivative gas turbines has jumped as large data center developers increasingly seek behind-the-meter (BTM) generation and avoid long lead times for larger gas turbine units.

Some 29.6 GW of behind-the-meter (BTM) gas generation will be added in the U.S. through 2030 and data centers will account for ​roughly 88% of demand, according to Enverus Intelligence Research. Data center developers are prioritizing faster development and are often willing to pay higher power prices to avoid grid ‌connection delays.

Soaring demand and a shortage of manufacturing capacity for larger gas turbines has led to rising costs and long lead times. Small gas turbines include aeroderivative turbines derived from aircraft engines, industrial gas turbines and microturbines. Many large-scale data center developers have opted for aeroderivatives as they offer rapid deployment and modular installation.

Lead times for large combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) plants can stretch up to six years while small or medium frame turbines can be delivered within two years and aeroderivatives ​in around 40 months, according to Enverus. Suppliers include GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Power for large-frame turbines; GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Baker Hughes for aeroderivatives; and Caterpillar, Wartsila and ​Innio Jenbacher for reciprocating engines.

Smaller turbines also have lower capital costs then larger units and can be installed incrementally in line with data center expansions.

“We’ve secured ⁠turbine supply through direct partnerships with turbine and equipment manufacturers including GE Vernova and Bergen,” John Adams, SVP, Power Infrastructure at AI infrastructure company Crusoe, told Reuters Events.

Crusoe has ordered 29 GE Vernova 35 ​MW aeroderivative gas turbines in a move towards BTM generation at U.S. data centers, including ten units for its Abilene, Texas campus. In June, Crusoe agreed to procure around 750 MW of Bergen reciprocating gas engines ​for on-site generation at multiple U.S. data-center sites.

CHART: US oil or gas-fired powergen in advanced development, by supplier

(Sample, August 2026)

Siemens Energy has seen rising demand across its gas turbine range, Matt Neal, President of Siemens Energy North America, told Reuters Events.

"Some customers buy several smaller turbines for earlier availability, flexibility and redundancy," Neal said.

“As a general rule, the larger ​a machine is, the longer it takes to manufacture and install," he said.

Cost equation

A shortage in manufacturing has driven up the cost of new large CCGT units.

In one example, Duke Indiana has estimated the ​cost of its planned 1.5 GW Cayuga CCGT project at $3.3 billion, some $900 million more than it assumed for new gas-fired capacity in general in 2024.

Join 1,500+ senior decision-makers across energy and finance at Reuters Events Energy LIVE 2026.

While large ‌CCGTs have ⁠higher capital costs than smaller turbines they are more efficient, offering lower average costs over the lifetime of the plant.

Capital costs per unit of electricity can be up to 50% higher for smaller turbines, Bobby Noble, Senior Program Manager, Gas Turbines & Emerging Fuels at the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI), told Reuters Events.

"The upfront cost of purchasing, installing and maintaining these technologies must be weighed against the cost per MWh over the plant’s lifetime,” Dan O’Beirne, Interim Project Manager, Global Oil & Gas Plant Tracker at Global Energy Monitor, said.

Large CCGTs also have lower greenhouse gas emissions per MWh because smaller open-cycle units have “lower firing temperatures and no ​heat recovery system,” he said.

Meanwhile, turbine manufacturers are ​expanding U.S. production capacity for larger turbine models ⁠which will start to curb cost increases and shorten lead times.

GE Vernova is investing $160 million to expand its Greenville, South Carolina factory by 2028, adding 650 workers, while Siemens Energy is restarting its factory in Charlotte, North Carolina by 2028.

Expanded U.S. manufacturing capacity will help some developers switch from buying turbines from overseas ​and avoid import tariffs and steel duties, Heather Leahey, principal analyst at Enverus, said.

Future value

Some data center developers are installing small gas-fired or hybrid BTM ​power solutions to provide near-term ⁠load until larger permanent power solutions are built or a grid connection becomes available. On-site generation assets can be used to support the data center and local grid needs in the future.

Larger and newer gas-fired turbines are "more suited to eventually become a merchant grid asset” because lower marginal costs mean they retain more value, Jack Painter, Vice President at consultancy Capstone, told Reuters Events.

“Developers also care about the emissions profile, given that some of the ⁠final customers care ​about it,” he said.

For exclusive energy insights, sign up to our newsletter.

Utilities and large customers could look to alternative sources to ​gas turbines that can be deployed incrementally, such as virtual power plants, batteries, repowering with clean power assets and hybrid resources, as well as grid enhancements and energy efficiency savings, Mark Dyson, Managing Director at Electricity at research group Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI), told ​Reuters Events.

“Near-term alternatives could meet nearly all projected near-term U.S. load growth, while reducing exposure to turbine shortages and avoiding some of the reliability and affordability risks associated with waiting for new gas generation," he said.

novelty.reason: Reference View covered severe large-turbine and transformer supply constraints, but not the emerging small-turbine and reciprocating-engine route, its quantified 29.6 GW BTM buildout, or the named Crusoe procurement commitments.

policy.reason: The message does not satisfy the existing alternative-firm-power Policies because it does not identify a Bloom-associated project switching routes or a commercially operating alternative on a required schedule. It is nevertheless relevant as an uncovered upstream change to the alternative-supply window.

expert_trade.expectation_delta: The report moves alternative gas power from a general reservation signal toward a sizeable, modular, faster-deploying route: approximately 29.6 GW of U.S. BTM gas additions through 2030, 88% tied to data centers, small or medium turbines deliverable within two years, aeroderivatives in roughly 40 months, and named Crusoe purchases of 29 GE Vernova units plus about 750 MW of Bergen engines. This shortens the expected duration of Bloom’s time-to-power advantage and raises the probability that future load is allocated to gas alternatives.
expert_trade.prior_expectation: BE’s opportunity window relied on grid and large-gas-turbine delivery constraints, with gas turbines previously described as sold out for three to four years and reservations not yet equivalent to local operating capacity. Bloom had customer validation and contracted/deploying capacity, but future share depended on alternatives remaining unavailable on required schedules.
expert_trade.reason: TRADE/SHORT: the path is alternative availability → customer firm-power route selection → lower future Bloom share and replacement-pipeline duration. The scale, delivery timing, named orders, and planned U.S. manufacturing expansion are material to BE’s core AI-power thesis even without a current Bloom project cancellation. No commercial operation or Bloom-associated project switch limits magnitude, while higher lifetime cost and emissions preserve some Bloom opportunity.

candidate.proposition: OpenAI is implementing protocols that separate reinforcement-learning graders from a model’s chain of thought to detect or prevent metagaming and eval-awareness.
OpenAI’s new frontier-model training framework requires a documented safety case showing that risks are understood and controlled before a training run continues.
OpenAI’s framework grants senior leaders authority to veto training runs, escalates critical failures to the CEO, and prohibits humans and AI agents from disabling monitoring systems.
Alphabet is legally challenging two European regulatory mandates that would require Google to open Android and its search-results index to market rivals.
One challenged EU mandate would require Google to open Android to artificial-intelligence tools such as OpenAI.
Google argues that the challenged EU access requirements would undermine existing privacy safeguards and cause irreversible harm to users in Europe.
candidate.subject_time: Google’s position in current EU litigation

candidate.proposition: OpenAI’s revised $200 Pro subscription is scheduled to provide 50% of the prior proportional API spending value when enrollment reopens.
OpenAI plans not to restore the previous five-hour rate limit for the $200 Pro plan’s weekly usage allocation.
OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna at API prices equal to 50% of their previous prices.
OpenAI plans to introduce subscription features that do not consume users’ API usage quotas.
Nvidia is negotiating with insurers on financial structures that would help smaller cloud providers and AI startups finance purchases of Nvidia GPUs.
The proposed insurance structures would protect lenders against losses if a neocloud customer defaults and pledged GPUs cannot be resold for enough to repay the loan.
Nvidia is sharing data on compute pricing and chip depreciation to support treating GPUs as a high-value investable asset class comparable to commercial aircraft financed against residual value.
Nvidia stated that the insurance discussions are early and may not result in a completed deal.
Enverus estimates that approximately 29.6 GW of behind-the-meter gas generation will be added in the United States through 2030, with data centers accounting for roughly 88% of demand.

Enverus estimates that large combined-cycle gas-turbine plants can have lead times of up to six years, while small or medium-frame turbines can be delivered within two years and aeroderivative turbines in approximately 40 months.
Crusoe ordered 29 GE Vernova 35 MW aeroderivative gas turbines for behind-the-meter generation at U.S. data centers, including ten units for its Abilene, Texas campus.
Crusoe agreed to procure approximately 750 MW of Bergen reciprocating gas engines for on-site generation at multiple U.S. data-center sites.
candidate.subject_time: Crusoe multi-site U.S. data-center generation program

candidate.proposition: GE Vernova plans to invest $160 million to expand its Greenville, South Carolina factory by 2028 and add 650 workers, while Siemens Energy plans to restart its Charlotte, North Carolina factory by 2028.

The Rocky Mountain Institute stated that near-term alternatives including virtual power plants, batteries, clean-power repowering, hybrid resources, grid enhancements, and energy efficiency could meet nearly all projected near-term U.S. load growth.
The forthcoming book The AGI Chronicles reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei first met in May 2022 at a dinner concerning Anthropic’s compute needs.
The book excerpt alleges that Anthropic chief compute officer Tom Brown presented a spreadsheet arguing that Google TPUs were a better dollar-for-dollar investment than Nvidia GPUs.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that Jensen Huang called Anthropic executive Tom Brown a “bean counter” during the reported meeting.
candidate.subject_time: Nvidia response to the reported 2022 meeting

candidate.proposition: Anthropic later formed a partnership with Nvidia and currently uses a mix of Nvidia and AMD GPUs, Google TPUs, and custom inference chips under development.
The AGI Chronicles is scheduled for release on October 6, 2026.
McDonald's uses a machine-learning pricing engine to analyze millions of daily transactions across nearly 14,000 restaurants and generate location- and item-level price recommendations.
In January 2026, McDonald's began requiring franchisees to be constructively engaging with approved pricing consultants and tools under new business standards.
McDonald's pricing-portal terms warn that franchisees may be competitors and should comply with antitrust and competition laws.
Meta launched a Muse AI suite for small businesses with Stripe integration that lets users update prices, create products, issue refunds, and analyze revenue trends.
Muse connects to external productivity applications including Slack, QuickBooks, Asana, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, and Zoom to execute business actions.
Approximately one-third of Muse users had already linked the AI to Facebook pages or Instagram business profiles in early usage trends.
candidate.subject_time: Early Muse usage as of September 2026

candidate.proposition: Meta is shifting Muse from a consumer-focused agent toward small-business use.

Former NVIDIA Technical Advisory Board member Eric Gullichsen publicly claimed that his September 9, 1993 grant of 25,000 NVIDIA stock options was intended to vest fully within one year rather than over four years.
Eric Gullichsen said NVIDIA rejected a proposed settlement concerning the alleged 1993 option-vesting discrepancy.
candidate.subject_time: Settlement discussions concerning the 1993 option grant

AU Optronics showcased a MicroLED optical-communication design at SEMICON Taiwan 2026 with a target interconnect range of up to 10 meters for AI data-center applications.
Bloom Energy shares rose approximately 2% in early premarket trading on September 29, 2026.
AMD's EPYC 9006 (Venice) server-CPU lineup was reported with list prices ranging from $700 to $14,904 across SP7 and SP8 SKUs.
AMD's EPYC 9006 SP7 platform is scheduled to launch in Q4 2026, and the SP8 platform is scheduled to launch in the first half of 2027.
candidate.subject_time: SP7 launch in Q4 2026; SP8 launch in H1 2027

candidate.proposition: TD Cowen initiated coverage of SpaceX with a Buy rating and a $200 price target.
TD Cowen forecasts that terrestrial AI-compute leasing will become SpaceX's fastest-growing business and the majority of its total revenue by the first quarter of 2027 as capacity ramps.
Anthropic reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $4.59 billion, up 1,088% from approximately $386 million in 2024.
Anthropic reported a FY2025 GAAP net loss of approximately $41.97 billion, including roughly $34 billion of non-cash accounting charges tied to financing convertible into Anthropic shares.
Anthropic's FY2025 compute and infrastructure spending rose 190% to approximately $7.33 billion, equal to 58% of its approximately $12.65 billion of total operating expenses.
Anthropic's IPO prospectus outlines approximately $518 billion of cloud, compute, and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.
Anthropic's preliminary second-quarter revenue exceeded $11.5 billion.
Anthropic's annual recurring revenue reached approximately $65 billion by late July 2026.
Anthropic's prospective IPO could value the company above $2 trillion, potentially after the November 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

Sony Store Japan announced that PS5 Pro purchase-lottery applications require a Sony account registered in Japan and at least 60 total hours of gameplay on a PS4 or PS5 during the two-year period ending September 27, 2026.

candidate.subject_time: PS5 Pro Japan purchase-lottery application opening

candidate.proposition: USB-IF's Integrators List includes Intel's Nova Lake-H mobile platform device IDs D331 and D333 as compliant with the USB4 80 Gbps specification.
PCI-SIG's Integrators List includes Intel's 900-series chipsets for Core Ultra 400-series Nova Lake-S processors.
Recent leaks point to Intel Core Ultra 400-series Nova Lake desktop and laptop processors launching in the first quarter of 2027.

OpenAI reported that AI was used in implementation, design-space exploration, verification loops, and arithmetic-circuit optimization for its Jalapeño chip, enabling a nine-month path from initial design to tapeout.
OpenAI reported that AI-assisted Jalapeño designs improved a BF16 multiplier by 56%, an FP4 dot-product block by 21%, and an FP32 accumulator by 10% versus human baselines.
Architect Labs claimed that its Redwood accelerator was almost entirely developed by AI after human architects defined the specification.
Architect Labs' Redwood accelerator has not been taped out as an ASIC and currently runs on an FPGA.
Architect Labs projects that a Samsung 8LPP implementation of Redwood could achieve a 3.4x performance-per-watt advantage over Nvidia's Jetson Orin Nano.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met with Senate Majority Leader John Thune on September 29, 2026, and Thune described the discussion as productive.
The White House and U.S. Senate leaders scheduled a collective meeting with leading AI executives for September 30, 2026, to discuss the future of artificial intelligence.
